question.:question/problem: Given that $y={e}^{3{x}^{2}-x},$ find $\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x}.$
question.:question/worked-solution:
First, we express $y$ as the composite function

$$
y={e}^{u},\,u=3{x}^{2}-x.
$$

Differentiating gives

$$
\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}u}={e}^{u},\,\frac{\text{d}u}{\text{d}x}=6x-1.
$$

We now apply the chain rule, and get

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x} & =\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}u}\cdot \frac{\text{d}u}{\text{d}x} \\  & ={e}^{u}\cdot (6x-1) \\  & =(6x-1){e}^{u} \\  & =(6x-1){e}^{3{x}^{2}-x}.\end{aligned}
$$
